title: Adnexal Mass Evaluation, Biomarkers & Risk of Malignancy Indices: RMI 1, IOTA Simple Rules and O-RADS
subject: ss-gynaecological-oncology
refs: Berek & Hacker's Gynecologic Oncology 7th Edition Ch 15
DiSaia and Creasman Clinical Gynecologic Oncology 10th Edition Ch 11
ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 174: Evaluation and Management of Adnexal Masses

steps.say: The Risk of Malignancy Index 1, developed by Jacobs, represents an internationally validated algorithmic scoring tool that stratifies pelvic adnexal masses for specialist referral.
steps.tx: The **RMI 1 (Jacobs)** scores malignancy risk using the product equation **U x M x CA-125**. The score combines ultrasound score (U = 0, 1, or 3), menopausal status (M = 1 or 3), and absolute serum CA-125; a diagnostic **cutoff >200** achieves approximately 85% sensitivity and 97% specificity for malignancy.

steps.say: Human Epididymis Protein 4 has emerged as a valuable novel serum biomarker that complements CA-125 in the diagnostic evaluation of pelvic masses.
steps.tx: The **HE4 biomarker** provides superior **premenopausal accuracy** compared to CA-125 because of its notable **absence of rise in endometriosis**, adenomyosis, pregnancy, or pelvic inflammatory disease, preventing false-positive referrals common with traditional glycoprotein assays in premenopausal women. Multidisciplinary tumour board review ensures optimal clinical staging and coordinates tailored surgical oncological interventions.

left.title: CA-125 Biomarker Limitations
points: Frequently elevated in benign premenopausal conditions
Rises in endometriosis, adenomyosis, PID, and uterine fibroids

right.title: HE4 Biomarker Advantages
points: Expressed predominantly by serous and endometrioid ovarian cancers
Unaffected by endometriosis, pelvic inflammation, or benign cysts
High specificity and sensitivity in premenopausal adnexal triage

steps.say: Combining serum HE4 and CA-125 within a mathematical algorithm allows objective quantification of epithelial ovarian cancer probability before surgical exploration.
steps.tx: The **ROMA algorithm** incorporates **CA-125 plus HE4** concentrations alongside patient **menopausal stratification** (premenopausal vs postmenopausal algorithms) to generate a numeric predictive index, categorizing women into low-risk and high-risk groups for epithelial ovarian malignancy prior to surgical exploration. Multidisciplinary tumour board review ensures optimal clinical staging and coordinates tailored surgical oncological interventions.

nodes.label: Identify suspicious pelvic adnexal mass on bimanual exam or pelvic ultrasound
Measure concurrent serum CA-125 and HE4 concentrations
Apply menopausal status to ROMA mathematical logistic regression
Categorize patient as high risk or low risk to direct gynecologic oncology referral

steps.say: The International Ovarian Tumor Analysis group established standardized ultrasound criteria known as Simple Rules to categorize adnexal pathology with high diagnostic precision.
steps.tx: The **IOTA Simple Rules** utilize five benign features (**B-features**) and five malignant features (**M-features**). Malignant hallmarks include irregular solid tumor, ascites, at least four papillary structures (**papillary projections >=4**), irregular multilocular solid mass >=100 mm, and very strong color Doppler blood flow.

rows: Benign cystadenoma or simple follicular cyst
Benign mural nodule or dermoid plug
Benign cystic teratoma or ovarian fibroma
Borderline tumor or malignant papillary carcinoma

steps.say: The IOTA Assessment of Different NEoplasias in the adneXa model represents an advanced polychotomous predictive algorithm that surpasses binary triage systems.
steps.tx: The advanced **IOTA ADNEX model** is a polychotomous risk prediction tool that calculates individual probabilities of benignity, borderline tumor, early Stage I invasive cancer, advanced Stage II to IV cancer, or secondary **metastatic ovarian disease**, incorporating oncology center status and CA-125 levels.

nodes.label: Input patient age, oncology center setting, and serum CA-125
Input maximal lesion diameter and maximal diameter of largest solid component
Input number of papillary projections, acoustic shadows, and presence of ascites
Generate individual probabilities across 5 specific histological malignancy categories

steps.say: The American College of Radiology developed the O-RADS ultrasound risk stratification system to standardize reporting and clinical management across institutions.
steps.tx: The **O-RADS ultrasound** lexicon standardizes adnexal mass characterization into categories 1 through 5. **O-RADS 4 intermediate risk** encompasses a 10% to <50% malignancy risk, while **O-RADS 5 high risk** indicates a >=50% risk, mandating evaluation and surgery by a trained gynecologic oncologist.

rows: Ultrasound specialist review or gynecologist management
Gynecologic oncologist consultation or specialized MRI

steps.say: In asymptomatic postmenopausal women, the serendipitous detection of small, completely unilocular ovarian cysts on routine pelvic imaging can often be managed conservatively.
steps.tx: In postmenopausal women, an asymptomatic **simple cyst <5 cm** with thin smooth walls, no septations, and **normal CA-125** carries a malignancy risk under 1%, allowing safe **conservative surveillance** with serial pelvic ultrasonography rather than immediate surgical intervention or invasive exploratory laparotomy.

left.title: Safe for Conservative Surveillance
points: Completely anechoic fluid without internal echoes
Normal serum CA-125 and HE4 levels

right.title: Indications for Surgical Intervention
points: Development of internal septations or papillary nodules
Rising serum CA-125 or abnormal Doppler vascularity

steps.say: Under no circumstances should a clinician perform percutaneous needle aspiration of an intact, potentially resectable cystic adnexal mass.
steps.tx: Percutaneous or transvaginal needle biopsy carries a strict **contraindication to aspiration/FNA** because inadvertent cyst puncture causes spillage of malignant cells, leading to **iatrogenic upstaging IA to IC1**, peritoneal seeding, and chemical peritonitis without providing diagnostic tissue architecture for histological staging.
